data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The sum of all possible values of n is 16592.","counterconditions":[{"case":"There exists a prime p such that p^20 < 12005.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"There exists a pair of distinct primes p, q such that p^6 * q^2 < 12005 and not covered by the listed pairs.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"n is not required to be a positive integer.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Let m = n + 2005. Since 1 <= n < 10000, we have 2006 <= m < 12005. An integer m has exactly 21 factors if and only if its prime factorization is of the form p^20 or p^6 * q^2 for distinct primes p and q. 1) For m = p^20, the smallest value is 2^20 = 1,048,576, which exceeds the upper bound. 2) For m = p^6 * q^2: If p=2, m = 64 * q^2. We need 2006 <= 64q^2 < 12005, so 31.34 <= q^2 < 187.58. Possible primes q are 7 (m=3136, n=1131), 11 (m=7744, n=5739), and 13 (m=10816, n=8811). If p=3, m = 729 * q^2. We need 2006 <= 729q^2 < 12005, so 2.75 <= q^2 < 16.45. Possible primes q are 2 (m=2916, n=911) and 3 (invalid, p must be distinct from q). If p >= 5, m = p^6 * q^2 >= 5^6 * 2^2 = 15625 * 4, which exceeds the upper bound. The possible values of n are {1131, 5739, 8811, 911}. Their sum is 1131 + 5739 + 8811 + 911 = 16592.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
